high_level_description: Wordless French compagnonnage workshop illustration: a builder assembles a timber arch over a full-scale art-du-trait épure, an independent reviewer checks the joints from the opposite side, and a project steward alone holds the final locking peg; precise ink-and-gouache drawing, natural oak, chalk blue and iron red, no text or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A tall carpentry hall has pale lime walls, exposed roof trusses, broad north-facing windows, and an unobstructed plank floor covered by a full-scale blue and red geometric épure. The construction lines use circles, arcs, perpendiculars, and intersections without pointed ends. Neutral daylight reaches the entire work. No letters, numbers, badges, inscriptions, diagrams, interface panels, directional symbols, or ceremonial signs appear.

elements.desc: Complex natural-oak demonstration arch standing at the center, assembled from six visibly interlocking curved members above the floor épure. Five joints are closed with plain wooden pegs; the sixth remains aligned but deliberately open. A simple test cradle suspends three equal iron weights from the crown while temporary side braces keep the structure stable.

Implementation carpenter with medium-brown skin, short dark curls, cream linen shirt, indigo waistcoat, ochre work trousers, red neckerchief, and black boots. Standing on the left with a focused expression, they fit the fifth joint using a wooden mallet and chisel while leaving the final open joint and its peg untouched.

Independent reviewer with light skin, long grey braid, indigo work coat, cream trousers, dark boots, and round spectacles. Standing alone on the right side, she checks the completed joints using a large wooden square and plumb line, facing the structure rather than the builder and carrying no mallet, spare peg, or publication seal.

Project steward with dark skin, close-cropped black hair, red work jacket, cream apron, indigo trousers, and black shoes. Kneeling in the clear foreground, he compares the arch to the floor intersections while holding the single final oak locking peg across both open palms, visibly separated from the builder's tools and the reviewer's instruments.
